adaptation: Standard layout adapted: the chart anchors on total money in (revenue $232.9M + non-cash warrant fair-value gain $1,034.4M = $1,267.2M) because the warrant gain is 4.4x revenue and a revenue-scaled chart cannot draw it. Net interest and other expense ($35.1M) is grouped with operating expenses, so the chart's operating line is the reported pre-tax income. Balance checks on the adapted model: total money in = left after direct costs + cost of revenue ($1,267.2M = $1,157.6M + $109.6M); left after direct costs = pre-tax income + operating expenses ($1,157.6M = $1,071.6M + $86.0M); pre-tax income - tax = net income ($1,071.6M + $106.5M tax benefit = $1,178.1M). Reported figures are unchanged: revenue $232.9M, gross profit $123.3M, operating income $72.4M, net income $1,178.1M.
verdict: Core Scientific's colocation revenue surged as AI data centers came online, lifting revenue 187% to $233M — while a $1.0B non-cash warrant gain turned the bottom line into a $1.18B profit.

On revenue alone, net income was $506 per $100 of revenue, again only because of the paper gain and tax benefit.
footerNote: Adapted layout — see one-time items. Figures in $M to three decimals so the lines add up exactly. Reported operating income was $72M.

takeaways.title: Colocation is taking over
takeaways.text: Colocation revenue rose nearly 60% in one quarter to $215M — 93% of all revenue — as 485 MW of capacity was billing at quarter end, representing over $700M of average annualized revenue. Total revenue was $233M, up 187% YoY, and colocation gross margin was 60%.

takeaways.title: A paper gain made the profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $1,178M, but $1,034M of it was a non-cash gain as warrant liabilities fell in value, plus a $107M tax benefit. Strip those out and the operating business earned $72M. That is why diluted EPS ($0.47) is so far below basic EPS ($3.42).

takeaways.title: The underlying business improved
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled from last quarter to $134M, a 57% margin. Self-mining is shrinking fast (revenue down 79% YoY to $12M, at a -61% gross margin) as sites are repurposed for colocation — the segment mix is now almost entirely AI data centers.

oneTimers: Change in fair value of warrants and contingent value rights: +$1,034.4M — a non-cash paper gain (the warrants Core Scientific owes became cheaper as the share price moved). It is shown as a source in the chart, with the layout adapted and documented, because it is 4.4x revenue. Last quarter the same line was a $1,045.5M loss.
Income tax was a $106.5M benefit this quarter, mostly deferred — it added to the bottom line instead of reducing it.
Digital assets held were marked up by $19.3M (a gain inside operating results), partly offset by a $5.3M loss on disposing of equipment and a $1.5M write-down of assets held for sale.
